title: Matthew 24:29–31
context: After the suffering of those days, Jesus describes cosmic shaking, the sign of the Son of Man, worldwide mourning, and His cloud-coming in power and glory. Angels with trumpet gather together his chosen ones from the four winds—public, royal, and final for the hope of His people.

voices.heading: Voices from both camps
voices.intro: What earlier interpreters on each side wrote about Matthew 24:29–31.
voices.note: Quotations lightly abridged for length; wording follows standard English translations of the sources named.

arminian.quote: Immediately after the tribulation of those days - Here our Lord begins to speak of his last coming. But he speaks not so much in the language of man as of God, with whom a thousand years are as one day, one moment. Many of the primitive Christians not observing this, thought he would come immediately, in the common sense of the word: a mistake which St. Paul labours to remove, in his Second Epistle to the Thessalonians.
arminian.source: Explanatory Notes upon the New Testament (on Matt 24:29–31)

reformed.quote: And immediately after the tribulation of those days. Christ comes now to speak of the full manifestation of his kingdom, about which he was at first interrogated by the disciples, and promises that, after they have been tried by so many distressing events, the redemption will arrive in due time.
reformed.source: Commentary on a Harmony of the Evangelists (on Matt 24:29–31)

verses.text: “But immediately after the suffering of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken;
verses.arminianNotes:
Immediately after that tribulation, lights fail and heavens shake. Creation itself signals the next act.

Wesleyans hear a call to sober hope: the darkening is not meaningless terror. Grace invites readiness for the Son who comes after the shaking, not despair under the sky’s collapse.
verses.reformedNotes:
Cosmic disorder follows tribulation on Jesus’ timetable—“immediately after.” Sun, moon, stars, and powers answer His word.

The Creator who hung the lights also darkens them. Providence rules the heavens’ shaking as stage-setting for the Son of Man.

verses.text: and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
verses.arminianNotes:
The sign appears; tribes mourn; all see Him coming on the clouds with power and glory. No secret tip-off will be needed.

Mourning can still turn to faith for those who hear now. Grace offers Christ before the sky splits; the public coming vindicates the gospel already preached.
verses.reformedNotes:
Heaven’s sign, earth’s mourning, and cloud-coming with power and glory fulfill Daniel’s Son of Man vision under Jesus’ claim.

Every tribe will see what God has appointed. The glory is His; mourning meets majesty on a day no rumor can manufacture.
verses.keyContrast: Both confess a public, glorious coming. Arminians stress present gospel urgency before that day; Reformed commentators typically stress God’s appointed unveiling that every tribe will witness.

verses.text: He will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.
verses.arminianNotes:
Angels, trumpet, and gathering of His elect from everywhere. The separation is personal and complete.

Arminians rejoice that the gathered are Christ’s. Grace that called them also keeps them to this assembly; the trumpet is comfort for those who endure in Him.
verses.reformedNotes:
He sends angels; the trumpet sounds; the elect are gathered from the four winds.

Election and gathering meet here. The very Lord who chose them sends for them—none of His are lost in the cosmic shake.
verses.keyContrast: Both rejoice in the elect’s gathering. Arminians stress grace that sustains unto that assembly; Reformed readers stress God’s electing purpose executed by angelic gathering at Christ’s command.
